core.title: Give every concrete telemetry item exactly one owning product slice
core.given: A plan contains concrete tracking-plan items, each resolving to a logical telemetry artifact URN (the URN shape comes from the profile).
core.when: Any concrete tracking-plan item is authored, changed, or evaluated (including full-plan validation of unchanged items).
core.then: Ensure each item's logical artifact is declared in the production declaration of exactly one product slice (uniqueness is over distinct slices, not over entries within a slice), and the item's owner names that slice.
prefer: Declare the logical artifact on the producing slice's production declaration (the declaration may omit a contract), then set the item's owner to that slice.
Decide ownership in the plan first; treat the registry only as something that resolves against plan-declared ownership.
avoid: Concrete items whose artifact no slice's production declaration names (emitted by code no plan stands behind).
Declaring the same logical artifact in two product slices' production declarations (two authors, no arbiter).
An owner field that names a slice other than the declaring one, or relying on the registry to grant ownership.
Treating a slice-level duplicate-producer finding from another check as covering or exempting the item-level check; both apply.
core.why: Two producers make an emission contract a coincidence waiting to diverge; zero means no slice stands behind the observable outcome. Both are plan defects, caught at the item.
evidence: The plan-validation check reports no finding of this rule over the whole plan.
For each concrete item, exactly one product slice's production declaration names the logical artifact URN, and the item's owner names that slice.
verification: Per concrete item - all concrete items, not only changed ones - count the distinct product slices whose production declarations name the artifact: zero producers is a finding (no owner), more than one is a finding (ambiguous producers), and exactly one producer with an owner naming another slice is a finding (owner mismatch).

Duplicate producers may also be reported by another check at the slice level; this rule reports the same ambiguity at the item level. That other check is not an exemption or waiver: the item-level invariant applies regardless of whether the slice-level finding exists.
Scope: the check covers concrete tracking-plan items. A production declaration with no telemetry artifact named and no concrete item resolving to it is not examined by this rule.
Disposition strict, severity 2: every finding fails the check; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline are assumed.

Ownership is read from the plan, never granted by the registry; findings surface through the stack's convention runner (profile: enforcement.runner), while the validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details.

fires: A plan author adds a concrete tracking-plan item whose logical artifact no product slice's production declaration names.
Two product slices' production declarations both name the same logical artifact URN that a tracking-plan item resolves to.
A tracking-plan item's owner names a slice other than the one whose production declaration names its logical artifact.
A slice's production declaration is removed or renamed while concrete items still resolve to that artifact.
A full-plan validation (or an unrelated plan edit) evaluates an existing, unchanged tracking-plan item that has zero producers, multiple producers, or a mismatched owner.
Another check already reports the duplicate producer at the slice level; this rule still reports the affected item at the item level.
doesNotFire: A concrete item whose logical artifact is named by exactly one product slice's production declaration and whose owner names that slice.
A production declaration with no telemetry artifact named and no concrete tracking-plan item resolving to it.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the plan artifacts that carry the slices' production declarations live; the check scans these files.
URN shape of a logical telemetry artifact, used identically by tracking-plan items and by production declarations (proposed key).
How a plan artifact declares the logical artifacts a product slice produces, including the single-value-or-list form of the telemetry field (proposed key).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a wagon produce[] entry whose telemetry field (string or list) names the logical artifact URN telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}; contract may be null

profileRequirements.meaning: The tracking-plan item field naming the product slice accountable for the artifact, and the slice identifier it names (proposed key).
profileRequirements.bunValue: the tracking-plan item field naming the wagon slug accountable for the artifact

profileRequirements.meaning: The tool that runs this check and through which its findings surface.

bunOnly.text:

  # plan/commons/_commons.yaml
  produce:
    - name: commons:response-invocation
      contract: null
      telemetry: telemetry:commons:response-invocation-accepted
bunOnly.reason: A project-specific worked example in the stack's plan-artifact syntax (a concrete path and concrete URN); the neutral core carries the obligation, and bun.json itself remains the reference example.

bunOnly.text: duplicate producers at the wagon level are also reported by planner.wagon.telemetry-filesystem under the planner profile; this rule reports the same ambiguity at the item level under the telemetry profile
bunOnly.reason: Names another rule's finding id and the stack's profile machinery; the core describes the overlap generically as 'another check at the slice level' and keeps the non-exemption in core:verification.
The parenthetical names the stack's profile grouping; the neutral core says 'a slice-level duplicate-producer finding from another check'.

bunOnly.text: Validator planner_telemetry_plan reports no planner.telemetry.logical-ownership finding over the whole plan.
bunOnly.reason: Validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core states the evidence generically (no finding of this rule over the whole plan).

bunOnly.text: finding values ["planner.telemetry.logical-ownership"]; note names validator planner_telemetry_plan and the telemetry profile
bunOnly.reason: The finding id belongs to this rule's realization; the core's verification describes the per-item findings generically, so the core activation has no finding fact.

classification.note: Situation neutral except the artifact URN shape telemetry:{theme}:{artifact}, which moves to the profile key urn.telemetry.
Already stack-neutral; phrasing (authored, changed, or evaluated, including full-plan validation of unchanged items) preserved so the change signal stays optional, not a prerequisite.

Obligation neutralized: exactly one declaring product slice plus owner names that slice; produce[] telemetry (string or list) and wagon slug are supplied by the two idiom keys. Uniqueness-over-distinct-slices nuance kept.
Rationale neutral: wagon -> product slice; 'caught at the item' preserved.

Neutral recommendation (declaration may omit a contract; set owner to the declaring slice); the concrete telemetry: telemetry:{theme}:{artifact} syntax and slug come from the profile idioms, and the concrete worked example stays in the realization (verifier_detail[4]).
Already stack-neutral: ownership decided in the plan; the registry only resolves against plan-declared ownership.
Zero-producer smell neutralized: wagon's produce[] -> any slice's production declaration.
Two-producer smell neutralized: two wagons' produce[] -> two product slices' production declarations.
Owner-mismatch and registry-grants-ownership avoidance neutralized; the owner/slug field shape is the profile idiom.
Non-exemption of the item-level check kept neutrally ('another check'); the '(planner profile)' reference is stack profile machinery and is recorded in bunOnly.
Generic no-finding-over-the-whole-plan evidence; the validator and finding ids (planner_telemetry_plan, planner.telemetry.logical-ownership) are realization details.
Per-item positive evidence neutralized; declaration and owner field shapes come from the profile idioms.

Term 'ownership_declaration': the concrete declaration shape (produce[] telemetry, string or list) and the URN shape go to the profile keys and define what the check counts (verification entry 1); 'ownership lives in the plan, not in the registry' is already carried by prefer[1] and avoid[2].
Term 'owner': the owner-must-equal-declaring-slice requirement is the core obligation (then) and the comparison in verification entry 1; the field/slug shape is the profile idiom.
Per-item counting algorithm over all concrete items (0 / >1 / owner mismatch), with uniqueness over distinct declaring slices, restated stack-neutrally in verification.
Overlap is a scope fact, not an exemption: kept in verification and avoid[3]; the other rule's id and profile names are realization details (bunOnly).
Project-specific fix-hint example in Bun plan syntax; it instantiates core:prefer[0], and the concrete YAML stays only in the realization.
Severity 2 and disposition strict are per-rule verification facts, not profile keys; strict is described generically (fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).

The path_glob fact is re-expressed as file_kind plan_artifact (path_glob is not a neutral fact type); the concrete glob plan/**/*.yaml comes from the profile. The Bun note that this identifies slice plans only, not tracking-plan items, is preserved by the separate tracking_plan_item fact below.

file_kind tracking_plan_item kept (a neutral plan-artifact kind); needs_new_observer preserved - path alone does not identify items, an observer must recognise concrete items and resolve each to its URN.
Phases plan_validation/plan_authoring are stack-neutral; the invariant applies whenever the plan is authored or validated, including full-plan checks.

Change signals neutralized (produce_telemetry_changed -> production_declaration_changed); they remain optional signals, not prerequisites - the 'when' clause and verification entry 1 keep unchanged items in scope.

The finding-id fact is a realization detail; the generic statement that the check reports zero/multiple producers or owner mismatch per item lives in core:verification, so the core activation carries no finding fact.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral already: it is an invariant over plan artifacts, so only terminology needed generalising. 'Wagon' became 'product slice' (the vocabulary's own gloss of a wagon as 'a bounded slice of the product'); the binding back to 'wagon', 'slug' and the produce[]-with-telemetry (string or list) construct lives in the two proposed idiom keys, since the closed vocabulary has no plan-artifact declaration or owner-field keys. 'Tracking plan' and 'registry' are kept as neutral telemetry concepts. The neutral activation-fact schema has no note field, so two Bun notes are preserved structurally instead: (a) the plan-artifact path identifies slice plans but not tracking-plan items - expressed by the separate tracking_plan_item fact with needs_new_observer; (b) change facts are optional signals, not prerequisites - expressed by the 'when' clause and by 'all concrete items, not only changed ones' in verification. The finding/validator ids of this rule and the other rule's slice-level overlap ids remain in bunOnly per the notProfileKeys rule. Neutral fact types do not include path_glob, so the plan/**/*.yaml fact is re-expressed as file_kind plan_artifact with the glob supplied by roles.plan_artifact.path.
